Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 29048 of 2023
Applicant :- Zakir Ali And Another
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And

Another Counsel for Applicant :- Niraj Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Gajendra Kumar,J.
Heard learned counsel for applicants and the learned A.G.A. for State.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants to quash/ stay the entire proceeding of Criminal Complaint Case No. 178 of 2018 (Noor Jahan vs. Jakir Ali & others), under Sections 420, 120B IPC, P.S. Maudaha, District Hamirpur as well as impugned orders dated 18.01.2021 and 18.08.2022 passed by court below.

sentences.text: Submission of learned counsel for the applicants is that the whole prosecution story is nothing but a counter blast to the earlier FIR which has been lodged by the applicants in which charge sheet has been submitted by investigating officer against opposite party no. 2.
It is a case of malicious prosecution and the entire proceeding is nothing but abuse of the process of law, therefore, the present proceeding as well as summoning order may be quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Per contra, learned A.G.A. submitted that the applicants have been summoned in the complaint case on the basis of material collected during inquiry and the statements recorded under sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.
At this stage, it cannot be adjudicated upon that this proceeding is malicious one and the applicants have been summoned after due inquiry in the complaint case.
From the perusal of material on record and looking into the facts of the case at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicants.
All the submissions made at the bar relates to the disputed question of fact, which cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

At this stage only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court in cases of R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R. 1960 S.C. 866, State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 192 and lastly Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another (Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cr.)
283.

sentences.text: The disputed defence of the accused cannot be considered at this stage.

Moreover, the applicants have got a right of discharge under Section 239 or 227/228 Cr.P.C. as the case may be,
before the court below and they are free to take all the submissions in the said discharge application before the trial court.
The prayer for quashing the proceedings of case as well as summoning order is refused.
At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submit that applicants may be permitted to move discharge application before the court concerned.

Keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, it is directed that the applicants will move a proper application for discharge through counsel within three weeks from today and they are free to take all the submissions in the said discharge application before the Trial Court which shall be considered and disposed of by the Trial Court in accordance with law within a period of one month.
Accordingly, the present application is disposed of.
For a period of three weeks no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants.

283.

Accordingly, the present application is disposed of.
